findings.current: To them, I had been a Benefactor, a trusted superior, and a comrade they could turn their backs to.
findings.defect: The English reverses the trust idiom: 등을 맡길 수 있는 means entrusting one’s exposed back to a comrade, not turning one’s back on or away from them.
findings.rationale: The source specifically characterizes Taekyung as someone they trusted to protect them in combat.
findings.replacement: To them, I had been a Benefactor, a trusted superior, and a comrade they could trust to watch their backs.
findings.source: 나는 그들에게 있어 은인이었고, 신뢰하는 상관이자 등을 맡길 수 있는 전우였다.

findings.current: I had been a blood brother, too.
findings.defect: “Blood brother” commonly denotes sworn brotherhood and leaves the actual biological kinship unclear.
findings.rationale: The preceding memories are of Taekyung’s biological brother, and 피를 나눈 형제 explicitly invokes shared blood.
findings.replacement: I was also his brother by blood.

findings.defect: The displayed contact name does not use the established translation.
findings.rationale: 명품충 is fixed in the supplied glossary as Designer-Brand Junkie.

findings.current: “I’ll make him one of my people. Even if I have to pay him three personal visits.[^1]”
findings.defect: The established name of the historical allusion is paraphrased rather than preserved.
findings.rationale: 삼고초려 is fixed in the supplied glossary as Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage, and the following Zhuge Liang joke depends on that allusion.
findings.replacement: “I’ll make him one of my people. Even if it takes Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage.[^1]”

findings.defect: Taekyung’s established squad title and Hyuk Mujin’s form of address are rendered inconsistently.
findings.rationale: The supplied glossary fixes 조장, specifically Hyuk Mujin’s address for Taekyung, as Captain.

findings.current:
For many years he had carried two swords. One at his chest, the other at his waist.

There was no need for more words.
findings.defect: The first sword is metaphorically harbored in the Head Elder’s heart, but the English places a second physical sword at his chest.
findings.rationale: 가슴에 품었다 contrasts the concealed purpose he has carried within himself with the actual sword at his waist.
findings.replacement:
For many years, he had carried two swords: one in his heart, and one at his waist.

There was no need for more words.
findings.source: 오랜 세월 두 자루의 검을 품었다. 하나는 가슴에, 하나는 허리춤에. 이제 더는 말이 필요 없었다.

findings.defect: The established Murim unit is converted into an explanatory quantity instead of using its fixed term.
findings.rationale: 갑자 is fixed in the supplied glossary as jiazi.

findings.current: His aim was to lay the foundation for a prestigious house that would one day be recognized even in the Central Plains.
findings.defect: The established Murim category 세가 is replaced with a generic description.
findings.rationale: 세가 is fixed in the supplied glossary as great family.
findings.replacement: His aim was to lay the foundation for a great family that would one day be recognized even in the Central Plains.
findings.source: 장차 중원에서도 인정받는 세가(世家)의 초석을 다지고자 했다.

findings.current: Whether in one form or half a form, the old man in front of him was a master a league above Lee Cheonbaek.
findings.defect: “Whether in one form or half a form” is incoherent English and loses the source’s measurement of the old man’s superiority by a full or half move.
findings.rationale: The source says that regardless of whether the margin was one full form or half a form, the Head Elder was the superior master.
findings.replacement: Whether by a full form or half a form, the old man before him stood above Lee Cheonbaek.
findings.source: 일 초식이건, 반 초식이건 눈앞의 노인은 이천백보다 윗줄의 고수였다.

findings.defect: Two named sects are rendered under non-established names, obscuring their identities within the Five Gates of Shanxi.
findings.rationale: 삼도문 and 궁귀문 are fixed in the supplied glossary as Samdo Sect and Gunggui Sect.
findings.replacement: The martial artists of the small and mid-sized sects known as the Five Gates of Shanxi—the Samdo Sect, a union of three sects; the Tao-centered Byeokdo Sect; and the Gunggui Sect, which had been pouring arrows from the cliffs without pause—turned in an instant.
findings.source: 세 개의 문파 연합체인 삼도문, 도를 중심으로 수련하는 벽도문, 절벽에서 쉴 새 없이 화살을 쏘아 대던 궁귀문까지.

summary: The block is broadly faithful, but several established names and ranks are inconsistent with the glossary, and a few passages materially blur kinship, trust, metaphor, or combat comparison.
